Get Wikidata items for a location

Source: R/get_wikidata.R
get_wikidata.Rd

Use the Wikidata Query Service to get items with coordinates (property P625) within a radius of a location. The search uses the wikibase:around SPARQL service. See https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikidata_Query_Service/User_Manual and https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:SPARQL_query_service/queries for more information.

Usage

get_wikidata(
  location,
  dist = getOption("getdata.dist"),
  diag_ratio = getOption("getdata.diag_ratio"),
  unit = getOption("getdata.unit", "meter"),
  class = NULL,
  subclasses = TRUE,
  limit = NULL,
  lang = getOption("getdata.lang", default = "en"),
  geometry = TRUE,
  crs = getOption("getdata.crs", 3857)
)

Arguments

location

sf object. If multiple areas are provided, they are unioned into a single sf object using sf::st_union()

dist, diag_ratio, unit

Radius of the search area around the center of location and the unit for the distance. If diag_ratio is provided, dist is set to the diagonal distance of the location bounding box multiplied by the ratio.

class

A character vector of Wikidata class identifiers (e.g. "Q41176" for building) used to filter items by "instance of" (property P31). Defaults to NULL for no filtering.

subclasses

If TRUE (default), include items that are an instance of a subclass (property P279) of class. Searching subclasses can make the query slower.

limit

Maximum number of items to return. Items are ordered by distance from the center of the location. Defaults to NULL for no limit.

lang

Language for item labels and the Wikipedia article URL; defaults to "en". Items without a label in lang use the English label.

geometry

If TRUE (default), return sf object. If FALSE, return a data frame with lon and lat columns.

crs

Coordinate reference system for the returned data. Only used if geometry = TRUE.

Value

A data frame or sf object with one row per item and columns for qid, label, dist (in meters), height (in meters), instance_of, and wikipedia. If no items are found, an empty data frame is returned with a warning.

Details

Compared to get_wiki_data(), which searches Wikipedia articles, this function can filter by what an item is (class) and returns the item identifier, the "instance of" labels, the Wikipedia article URL (if any), and the height (property P2048), if available. Height values are reported by Wikidata contributors, are missing for most items, and may not describe the highest point of a structure, so check them before using them in an analysis. This function does not return other properties or qualifiers. For those, use a package like tidywikidatar with the returned qid values.

The search area is always a circle. If dist is NULL and diag_ratio is NULL, the circle is the smallest circle around the center of the bounding box for location that includes the corners of the bounding box. If location is a point, dist or diag_ratio must be provided.

Examples

bmore_city_hall <- sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_point(c(-76.6122, 39.2904)),
  crs = 4326
)

# Get items within 500 meters of a point
get_wikidata(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  dist = 500,
  limit = 10
)
#> New names:

#> Simple feature collection with 10 features and 6 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT

# Filter by class. "Q41176" is building; subclasses like skyscraper and city
# hall are included by default.
get_wikidata(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  dist = 1,
  unit = "km",
  class = "Q41176",
  limit = 10
)

# Set subclasses = FALSE to only include items that are directly an instance of
# the class
get_wikidata(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  dist = 1,
  unit = "km",
  class = "Q41176",
  subclasses = FALSE,
  limit = 10
)

# Use a polygon to set the search area automatically
bmore_area <- sf::st_buffer(
  sf::st_transform(bmore_city_hall, 26985),
  dist = 300
)

get_wikidata(
  location = bmore_area,
  limit = 10
)

# Return a data frame instead of an sf object and use another language
get_wikidata(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  dist = 500,
  lang = "es",
  geometry = FALSE,
  limit = 10
)
